text:
deploy-bot: Promotion hold: release v3.12.1-pre. Artifact publish failed for wheel artifact `redwood_inference-3.12.1-py3-none-any.whl`. Registry response: 503 Service Unavailable. Promotion paused. See: https://ci.internal/logs/publish/1289

ada: getting this too. The publisher retried 3x then gave up. Hash present locally but remote manifest missing.

ryan: quick logs: ```
2026-03-21T16:12:02Z PUT /b/redwood-registry/o/redwood-inference/wheels/3.12.1/sha256:abc123 -> 503 Service Unavailable
2026-03-21T16:12:05Z PUT retry 1 -> 503
2026-03-21T16:12:20Z publisher: aborting after max retries
```

sam: is this a downstream GCS outage or our registry proxy? pkg-registry-bot shows no global incident.

pkg-registry-bot: No global outages reported. Partial region error: EU-WEST bucket reported elevated 5xx for ~10m. More details: https://status.cloud/gcs#eu-west-1 (note: internal link)

maya: release window is tight. Options: (A) retry publish with backoff; (B) re-run publisher targeting a different region/bucket; (C) hold promotion until registry stable. Which is least risky?

ada: we already tried automated backoff. I can trigger a cross-region publish fallback to US bucket if we decide to accept region divergence temporarily. That keeps artifact available for canary.

ryan: note: the wheel upload is signed and the registry verifies signature by path. If we duplicate to US bucket we must ensure rewrite preserves manifest and signatures. That path is simple: `publisher --target-bucket=us-wheels --preserve-digests`. I can run that after approval.

sam: alternative is to re-run the build to produce a new wheel and publish fresh; that would change the digest and require updating release notes/tags. More churn.

maya: I prefer fallback publish to US bucket to minimize churn and unblock canary. We should flag artifact as mirrored and follow up with a reconciliation job once EU is healthy.

ada: ok prepping fallback publish. Granting deploy permission to `ryan` to run cross-region push. Confirm?

ryan: running: `publisher push --artifact=redwood_inference-3.12.1-py3-none-any.whl --source=ci-cache/artifacts/1289 --target-bucket=us-wheels --preserve-digests`

[~2m later]

ryan: push completed. Registry responded 200 for US bucket. Item visible: https://us-wheels.internal/redwood_inference/3.12.1/sha256:abc123

deploy-bot: Artifact mirrored: US bucket. Promotion can proceed if staging smoke passes. Note: EU bucket still unhealthy; marking artifact as mirrored in release metadata.

sam: good. We'll need a short note in the release: "Artifact mirrored due to EU storage 5xx; reconciliation pending." I'll add it after canary.

maya: triggering canary promote with manual override: `deploy-bot promote --release v3.12.1-pre --target canary --force-artifact-mirror`

deploy-bot: Manual promote requested. Warning: artifact mirror in effect; proceed?

maya: proceeding. `yes`

deploy-bot: Canary promotion started. Notifying canary owners.

buildbot: canary jobs started. staging-smoke/7 queued on nodepool default.

[~14 minutes later]

buildbot: staging-smoke/7: PASS. integration-suite/11: PASS. No regressions in canary jobs.

maya: great, canary looks clean. Schedule prod rollout for next change window (2026-03-22 06:00 UTC) and include the mirrored-artifact note and mitigation steps in release notes.

ada: created ticket INF-4592 to reconcile EU bucket and audit publisher retries. Added PR #2401 which documents the fallback flow and a small publisher change to add region fallback automation.

ryan: we should also add an alert to deploy-bot when a publish uses mirror fallback so on-call sees it immediately. I'll include that in the PR.

pkg-registry-bot: Noted. EU GCS region recovered at 16:30 UTC. Starting background reconciliation: `reconcile-mirrors --artifact=sha256:abc123 --src=us-wheels --dst=eu-wheels`.

sam: once reconciliation succeeds we'll update release metadata and remove mirrored flag.

maya: thanks team. Closing thread once reconciliation and prod rollout complete. :thumbsup:
